page: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the m6a.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 10% on stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests. Its memory subsystem shows strong capabilities, with small-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching the top 10% and large-block read/write bandwidth in the top 25%. Computational workloads such as ray tracing, software compilation, and cryptography encryption tests also rank in the top 10% to top 25% tiers. However, single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and text processing, perform in the average middle 50% range.

Given its high resource density with 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM, the m6a.32xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale, multi-threaded enterprise applications that require balanced compute and memory resources without local storage requirements. The lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs represents a tradeoff for database-heavy or deep learning workloads. This instance is highly suited for multi-threaded application servers, high-throughput web serving, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices.
